rawContent: In the wake of the #MeToo movement, there are a lot of academics starting to study sexual violence for the first time. (Welcome!) I've been doing a lot of peer reviews and I see the same mistakes that mark you as a newcomer. Here's a checklist to avoid the obvious ones:

(2) Recognize that there have been some amazing feminist scholars doing this work for decades. Do NOT start your paper with, "Since the #MeToo movement..." Don't erase the contributions of the smart people who came before you.
YES. #MeToo is more than the way people talk about it in the media. Anyone doing anti-violence work absolutely must pay attention to Tarana Burke.

The reality is that most of the world is on our side. Most people think rape is a heinous crime. Most people want rapists to be held accountable. Following the #MeToo movement, more people than ever are eager for a change and want to support work like mine.

@Donnyappleseed_ Sure. I think this is some of the hard work of the #MeToo movement. We’re in a national conversation about how to balance the good with the violence. A lot of us are just tired of seeing the good eclipse any meaningful recognition of the violence. The violence matters.

@AleemKarmali @doctor_not_mrs I appreciate you saying that. If I learned anything from #MeToo, it was how much the general public really hungers for accurate and reliable information to make sense of sexual violence. It only seems right to provide what I have.
